verdict.rationale: Penpot documents an MCP server, outbound webhooks, and an API marketed for "workflow automation." These are building blocks that let external agents or apps drive automation. The evidence shows no first-party feature for setting up automations that run autonomously in the background, such as triggers, schedules, or rules executed by Penpot itself. The automation would live in the external agent or the system receiving the webhooks, so it earns no credit here.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background
